summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,520.93 on Nov 10 (-0.38%), about 4% below its record. It is still below a flattening 50-day average (~7,690) but holding above the 200-day (~7,325). October CPI ran hot: headline +0.4% m/m and core +0.3% against a 0.2% forecast. That pushed the 10-year to ~4.98% and Dec 9 FedWatch hike odds to roughly 89–100%, with ~10% odds of a 50bp move. The good news is that fragility has eased. VIX is ~19.5, back under 20 and falling from ~21 last week, breadth looks healthy (~61–69% of stocks above their 50-day), and HY spreads have stabilized at ~342bp. A 25bp December hike is now priced in, so the next tests are NVDA (Nov 17) and October PCE (Nov 25). Small entries in non-AI and equal-weight names are fine now. Hold AI-crowded adds until after NVDA, and treat a close below ~7,300 (the 200-day) as the trigger to flip to WAIT.
